summary: Kit seals complete provider configurations and optional Spotify credentials, using the backend recorded in each envelope. Sealing prefers available OS storage, then the weaker local identity-file fallback; the passphrase backend has no automatic settings unlock. Writes verify the seal and atomically rename an owner-only temporary file. Only a missing vault reads empty: read errors, malformed envelopes and malformed decrypted data refuse reads and subsequent saves. Narrow damaged-identity recovery preserves original files and reports the incident; cache and concurrent-write behavior are unchanged. The native keychain diagnostic uses a fresh probe-only namespace and reports cleanup failure, with isolated fake-tool regressions distinct from native platform proof. Guarded HTTP provider paths enforce configured-host redirect checks; external CLIs and MCP processes have separate network authority; model requests transmit selected conversation and observations, while the privacy ledger records usage rather than request contents. Studio Host, Origin, bearer and body gates protect the local API, while ungated token-bearing HTML relies on loopback reachability. Sandbox HTTP evidence does not establish packaged WebView isolation.

sections.title: Kit provider vault (shipping source preview)
sections.summary: Kit is a source preview with configured release-binary builds. The vault seals whole provider configurations, active selection and optional Spotify link. Backend-tagged opening prevents fallback to a different lock after decryption fails. Available Windows, macOS and Linux OS storage precedes the weaker identity-file fallback; passphrase setup is not exposed in settings. Saves verify a seal before private atomic replacement. Only ENOENT represents an absent vault; damaged envelopes, unreadable files and malformed decrypted rows refuse later saves instead of losing data. The narrowly defined damaged-identity recovery preserves both originals and reports the incident. Diagnostic keychain operations use their own invocation service and isolated fake-tool tests, which do not establish native-platform results. Provider egress, Spotify, recovery, cache and packaged-host limits are documented separately below.

children.title: What the vault seals
children.summary: The vault file stores a versioned backend-tagged ciphertext envelope under the configured Bunzai home. It encrypts the complete provider document, including keys, base URLs, extra headers, options, labels, active provider selection and optional Spotify link. Tests show provider names and keys are absent from the on-disk plaintext envelope. The decrypted document is cached in process memory after a successful open. Writes create an exclusive owner-only temporary sibling, verify that the chosen backend can reopen the new seal, sync file contents and rename it over the old vault. The containing directory is not fsynced. These operations protect replacement from a partial file write but do not establish cross-process revision-conflict handling for an already cached vault.
topics: mode 0600 at creation, file sync before rename, no directory sync

children.title: Backends and present platform boundary
children.summary: Opening follows the recorded backend. Sealing prefers DPAPI, macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service, then the weaker identity-file fallback; passphrase selection is not automatic. Keychain creation uses a cross-process lock, marker and fresh reads to avoid replacement. Values travel over stdin. Fake-tool tests cover locking and first seals. The native diagnostic uses a fresh service for both instances, locks and cleanup, reports failures and removes its temporary home. Child regressions preserve planted application credentials; native success requires recorded platform results. Holding both local identity file and vault permits decryption. Provider environment variables remain unpersisted alternatives.
topics: weaker than DPAPI and labeled so

children.title: Provider egress boundary
children.summary: Guarded HTTP model discovery and sends enforce configured-host checks; external Claude CLI and MCP network traffic bypass this HTTP guard. Every redirect hop retains the same host, prohibits HTTPS downgrade and obeys the five-hop cap. Credentials authenticate requests but stay outside conversations, tool observations and exports; privacy records reported usage, not all network traffic. Native Ollama metadata has 2 MiB, 512-model, four-worker and eight-second discovery bounds. One uncached resolution owns capabilities and context. Scene body overrides cannot replace num_ctx; malformed replies and unoffered Kit tools fail closed. These boundaries do not prove model quality, memory needs or packaged behavior.
topics: every redirect hop revalidated, five cap

children.title: The Spotify link (one more outbound authority)
children.summary: The Spotify tab adds two outbound hosts, accounts.spotify.com for tokens and api.spotify.com for the Web API, each behind its own guarded fetch that refuses a redirect elsewhere; the page cannot reach Spotify because its policy is connect-src self. The Client ID is the person's own app, there is no client secret, and sign-in is authorization code with PKCE. The redirect is the 127.0.0.1 loopback literal, on a route outside api gated only by a random single-use state. The refresh token is sealed in the key vault and never reaches preferences, logs, exports or model context; the access token is memory only. The routes are host-only. Proof is mocked network, not a live sign-in.
topics: accounts and api spotify hosts only
PKCE with the person's own Client ID
refresh token only in the key vault

children.title: Recovery limitations
children.summary: Unknown backends, wrong credentials and authentication failures throw. The sole recovery exception is an identity key structurally damaged and replaced during this open: key and unopenable vault are preserved, with an explanatory notice. Other failures remain untouched. Only ENOENT means absence; other file, envelope and plaintext-shape errors refuse later saves instead of becoming empty data. Legacy notice strings are accepted, but the current notice is process-derived. There is no export, rotation, backend-migration or recovery-key UI. Decrypted caching and cross-process write-conflict behavior are unchanged; parsing protection is not a concurrency guarantee.

sections.title: The loopback server (shipping)
sections.summary: Shipping code with automated Bun tests. The default visual app binds 127.0.0.1 only, and uploaded scripts remain data. A random per-launch bearer is injected into index HTML for trusted apiFetch and never handed to the sandbox. The api gate runs before every api handler, checks Host on every method, refuses cross-site GET and HEAD, and requires Origin plus token for POST and PATCH. JavaScript wasm CSS and icons are non-secret ungated assets. Index HTML is also ungated but contains the bearer, so its confidentiality relies on loopback reachability; any client that reaches the listener can read it. Reads remain weaker than mutations. Body caps are 64MB inspect and 32MB JSON.

children.title: The per-launch bearer
children.summary: A fresh bearer is minted once per launch as randomBytes(32).toString base64url in createSecurityContext marked never log or persist. injectSessionMeta puts it into served index HTML as an escaped meta name vaude-session which trusted apiFetch reads for API authentication. The token is never handed to the sandbox origin. The index document itself is not bearer-gated, so the default listener's loopback bind limits which machines can fetch it; any local client that reaches the listener can read the bearer.

children.title: The /api/* gate
children.summary: Every api route runs through checkApiRequest before its handler. JavaScript wasm CSS and icons are ungated. Index HTML is ungated too but carries the injected bearer, so it relies on the loopback bind. The api gate returns 503 before security context completion, checks Host on every method, and rejects attacker hostnames resolved to loopback. GET and HEAD carry no token and pass only for Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin or none; cross-site, same-site and unknown values are refused, and a Mozilla User-Agent with no header is refused on loopback. POST and PATCH require a loopback-equivalent non-null Origin and a timingSafeEqual token. Other methods return 405.

children.title: What the gate does not do
children.summary: Stated plainly because overclaiming would be a defect. localhost and ::1 on the correct port are accepted not rejected; only wrong port or foreign hostname fails closed. All three loopback spellings resolve to the same bound interface so rejecting localhost would paper-cut bookmarks while protecting nothing; the gate stops attacker hostnames not loopback aliases. GET and HEAD are not token-gated: a header-less non-browser client (curl, CLI, test) with no Sec-Fetch-Site passes the read gate. The read gate is deliberately weaker than the mutation gate. Reads that expose entity data rely on the loopback bind and the foreign-page refusal not on the bearer.

children.title: Body caps
children.summary: Request bodies stream with a hard byte cap and 413 on overflow: INSPECT_BODY_MAX 64MB JSON_BODY_MAX_BYTES 32MB in core media limits. readBodyCapped checks Content-Length early when present and enforces a running total as it reads so a lying or absent length header still cannot exceed the cap. Same fail-closed posture the upload adapters use against zip bombs.

sections.title: The sandbox origin (shipping code, packaged proof BLOCKED)
sections.summary: Untrusted Lua from the Risu Test Bench runs in a Worker from a second loopback listener on an ephemeral port, a distinct origin from UI and api. Defense-in-depth: same-origin Worker is a killable thread not an origin boundary so a future WebView or bundler bug would widen blast radius if same-origin. Fails closed by construction: serves only sandbox worker.js regex-worker.js and glue.wasm; every other path 404 with locked CSP; no api no index HTML no session token no traversal. CORS limited to exact UI origin plus loopback aliases so only trusted UI constructs the cross-origin module Worker. API token is never injected into anything this host serves. What is proven and what is not: allowlist CORS value-only wire API denial and token absence proven at Bun HTTP layer; packaged WebView2 isolation not measured; Plan 017 BLOCKED; do not claim fully isolated; same-origin fallback degraded not claimed isolated.

children.title: What is proven, and what is not
children.summary: Scaffolding additive to token Plan 005 and resource quotas Plan 016 not a replacement. Proven: allowlist CORS value-only wire API denial and token absence by Bun HTTP and handler tests. Not measured: packaged WebView2 origin isolation, whether WebView collapses two loopback authorities, crossOriginIsolated and storage separation, and credentialed API fetch from sandbox origin; Plan 017 BLOCKED until a WebView2 smoke matrix records those. Do not call the sandbox fully isolated sandboxed or exploit-proof. Until the matrix is green it is defense-in-depth with tested HTTP behavior and unmeasured in-WebView separation. Sandbox bind failure falls back to same-origin Worker explicitly degraded and not claimed isolated.
